zinc_source: U.S. Geological Survey, India minerals table, primary zinc smelter production in 2024 (817,058 t). https://www.usgs.gov/centers/national-minerals-information-center/india
jarosite_factor_note: About 0.5 t of jarosite residue per tonne of refined zinc, as cited from Kangas et al. (2017) in the source review. This draft does not remeasure the factor.

alternate_jarosite_supply_tpy.name: nandi_citation
alternate_jarosite_supply_tpy.note: Nandi and Ransinchung (2021) state that about 0.25 million tonnes of jarosite waste is released per year in India.

alternate_jarosite_supply_tpy.name: sharma_hzl_chittorgarh
alternate_jarosite_supply_tpy.note: Sharma (2021) states annual jarosite production of about 0.5 million tons from Hindustan Zinc at Chittorgarh, plus about 1.5 million tons accumulated. This is a plant-level claim, not a national mass balance.

hzl_use_note: Hindustan Zinc FY2023-24 environment report states 163,795 MT of jarosite used in cement construction. https://integratedreport.hzlindia.com/annual-integrated-report-fy-2023-24/environment.php
cement_co2_note: Central value is the Indian cement-sector intensity of 0.68 t CO2 per t cement in 2020 from the GCCA India roadmap executive summary. The high value is 0.90 t CO2 per t cement, the order of magnitude cited by Nandi and Ransinchung (2021) for cement production. OPC ground-to-gate figures of 0.91-1.00 t CO2e are reported by Basavaraj and Gettu (2025), doi:10.70002/iitm.rdr.1.1.37.
cement_price_note: Retail scenario built from publicly listed OPC bag prices of about Rs 370, Rs 400 and Rs 430 per 50 kg bag, converted to a tonne. This is not an ex-works or wholesale contract price.
carbon_price_note: India does not have one observed economy-wide carbon price in the sources used here. The none case is the reported central result. The other two values are labelled scenarios.
disposal_cost_note: No public hazardous-waste tipping fee was used. These three values are assumptions for sensitivity only.
transport_note: No measured haul or processing cost was used. These values are assumptions for sensitivity only.
jarofix_note: Gared and Gaur (2021) abstract: before disposal, 2% lime and 10% cement are added to make jarofix. Lime is recorded and not priced. The 10% cement credit is optional and is off in the central case, because the counterfactual disposal route is not observed for every tonne.
tclp_note: US toxicity-characteristic levels for lead, cadmium and silver. Zinc, copper and iron are not given limits here, because they are not on that list.
